KGC.physical_anchor: mines and pours gold doré/bullion at open-pit and underground operations across the Americas and West Africa
KGC.value_chain_position: mid-tier/senior gold producer selling doré for refining; minimal byproduct diversification

LIN.physical_anchor: produces and distributes industrial gases (oxygen, nitrogen, argon, hydrogen, CO2) from air-separation and steam-methane-reforming plants
LIN.value_chain_position: industrial-gas supplier under long-term on-site/pipeline contracts; not a rare-earth or strategic-metal separator/processor despite the Chemicals-Specialty industry tag

MT.physical_anchor: manufactures finished flat and long steel products (slabs, coils, rebar) at integrated steelmaking plants
MT.value_chain_position: steel converter selling finished steel products, not iron-ore/concentrate; captive ore feeds its own mills rather than being sold merchant — fails the diversified_miners revenue-source test the taxonomy names it under

MTRN.physical_anchor: mines beryllium ore at Spor Mountain, Utah and fabricates it (with copper, precious metals) into engineered alloys, clad strip and electronic coatings
MTRN.value_chain_position: vertically-integrated beryllium miner/refiner that converts most output into value-added advanced materials sold to aerospace/defense/semiconductor customers — majority of revenue is fabrication, not raw strategic-metal sales

MTUS.physical_anchor: melts scrap steel in electric-arc furnaces into engineered specialty steel bars and billets
MTUS.value_chain_position: specialty steel converter selling finished bar/billet products, not ore/concentrate — explicitly one of the taxonomy's named converter exclusions

NEM.physical_anchor: mines and pours gold doré, with meaningful copper concentrate byproduct, at open-pit and underground operations globally
NEM.value_chain_position: world's largest gold producer by output; senior producer with copper byproduct credits

NUE.physical_anchor: melts scrap steel via electric-arc-furnace mini-mills into finished long and flat steel products
NUE.value_chain_position: largest US steel producer selling finished steel, not iron ore/concentrate — explicitly named in the taxonomy as a converter to exclude from diversified_miners

OR.physical_anchor: holds royalty and stream contracts entitling it to a fixed percentage of gold and silver ounces poured at partner mines
OR.value_chain_position: royalty/streaming pure-play — no operating costs, direct claim on physical ounces produced by third-party mines

PAAS.physical_anchor: mines and produces silver/gold doré at primary-silver mines across the Americas
PAAS.value_chain_position: primary silver producer with significant gold byproduct credits; dominant_metal=silver

PPG.physical_anchor: manufactures paints, coatings and specialty chemical formulations at its own plants
PPG.value_chain_position: coatings manufacturer with no rare-earth or strategic-metal separation/processing exposure — a chemical-company false positive from the Chemicals-Specialty industry string

RGLD.physical_anchor: holds royalty and stream contracts entitling it to a fixed percentage of gold (plus silver/copper) ounces produced at partner mines
RGLD.value_chain_position: royalty/streaming pure-play, anchor example for the chain; auto-passes Lane A cash/profit gates

RIO.physical_anchor: mines and ships iron ore, copper concentrate/cathode, and bauxite/aluminum from operations on five continents
RIO.value_chain_position: diversified major (iron ore ~55% of revenue, copper, aluminum, minerals) — anchor example for both copper_mining and diversified_miners, legal two-chain membership within this book

RPM.physical_anchor: manufactures specialty coatings, sealants and roofing/building products (Rust-Oleum, DAP) at its own plants
RPM.value_chain_position: specialty coatings/sealants manufacturer with no rare-earth or strategic-metal exposure — a chemical-company false positive

RS.physical_anchor: buys finished steel and aluminum from mills, then cuts/processes to customer spec at its own service centers
RS.value_chain_position: metals distributor/processor (service center), not an ore/concentrate producer — explicitly named in the taxonomy as a converter to exclude

SBSW.physical_anchor: mines and refines platinum-group metals (platinum, palladium, rhodium) and gold at South African and US operations
SBSW.value_chain_position: PGM-and-gold producer with a growing battery-metals recycling adjacency; 'Other Precious Metals' industry proven live in this chain

SCCO.physical_anchor: mines and produces copper cathode and concentrate (plus molybdenum, zinc, silver byproduct) in Peru and Mexico
SCCO.value_chain_position: low-cost-quartile major copper producer, anchor example for the chain

SHW.physical_anchor: manufactures paints and architectural/industrial coatings at its own plants and sells through company-owned stores
SHW.value_chain_position: paints/coatings manufacturer with no rare-earth or strategic-metal exposure — a chemical-company false positive

SOLS.physical_anchor: manufactures fluorochemical refrigerants, specialty resins and electronic/semiconductor materials at its own plants
SOLS.value_chain_position: advanced-materials/specialty-chemicals manufacturer (2026 Honeywell spinoff) with no rare-earth mining, separation or magnet exposure — a chemical-company false positive

SQM.physical_anchor: extracts lithium carbonate and iodine from Atacama Desert brine deposits, plus potassium nitrate specialty plant nutrients
SQM.value_chain_position: brine-based lithium/iodine/potash producer — a genuine strategic-mineral miner, but lithium is outside this taxonomy's rare_earth_strategic thesis (rare earths, antimony, gallium, tungsten; no lithium chain exists in v2.0), so it doesn't ride a defined chain here

SSL.physical_anchor: converts mined coal and natural gas into synthetic fuels and chemicals via Fischer-Tropsch plants in South Africa
SSL.value_chain_position: integrated energy/chemicals producer (coal/gas-to-liquids); captive coal mining feeds its own conversion plants, not a merchant mining-chain commodity seller
